AFWD.justification: The transformation that maps the pair of sets to their algebraic sum A plus A

AREV.justification: The mapping from the sum set back to the constituent summands to verify membership

CLINK.justification: The sequential application of countable unions and intersections to build the hierarchy

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The boundary of the Borel hierarchy
ENGAGR.justification: The state where a set is simultaneously viewed as a limit of lower ranks and a base for higher ranks

EVALF.justification: The condition where the sum set fails to meet the criteria for the given sum-free set S

EVALT.justification: The condition where the sum set successfully falls within the required regularity or structure class

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the set A from its sum-free and non-sum-free components to verify its total Borel rank

FSPLIT.justification: The bifurcation of the set into elements that satisfy the sum-free property and those that do not

IFIX.justification: The fixed size of the set A which cannot be altered during the rank determination

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The identity of the set A
IMSCRIB.justification: The self-consistency of the set A as a fixed object throughout the evaluation

TANCH.justification: The final ordinal value that bounds the complexity of the set A

VINIT.justification: The state before the definition of the continuum or the subset A exists

phase_3.both_description: The undecidable state where the rank depends on the specific model of set theory
phase_3.false_description: There exists a sum-free set S such that A plus A is not in RS
phase_3.true_description: The sum A plus A is contained within the RS class for all S
phase_3.void_description: The undefined space before the selection of the subset A from the real line

steps.domain_action: define the real line as the base space
fix the cardinality of A to the power of the continuum
identify the candidate set A within the power set of the reals
apply the Borel hierarchy construction to A
branch on the sum-free property of an arbitrary set S
compute the Minkowski sum A plus A
evaluate the membership of A plus A in the class RS
discard S and select a new test set
return to the evaluation of A against all possible sum-free sets
hold the rank at the limit ordinal while checking all S
record the minimal rank that satisfies the condition for all S
output the minimal Borel rank as the final result
